positions.invalidation: Reduce or close if Canadian core inflation moves decisively above the current near-2% zone while employment and wage growth reaccelerate, or if BoC communication/delivered hikes validate a 2027 path in the mid-3% area. A headline-energy spike without confirmation in core inflation and labor is not sufficient invalidation.
positions.thesis: Receive the 2027 CORRA H/M/U/Z strip. The market prices roughly 84 to 130.5 bp of BoC tightening from a 2.29% overnight rate even though Canadian labor is weak and core inflation is near 2%; the 2027 hike cycle is too aggressive relative to the domestic reaction function.

pms.thesis: Hold the existing 2027 H/M/U/Z CORRA receive, but do not add. The exact strip has normalized materially in our favor to about 3.22 from the 3.40 entry, yet it still averages roughly 91bp above 2.31 cash and March alone remains around 2.945. Canadian underlying inflation near 1.95% and weak domestic labor still do not validate the full 2027 hike path. Brent near 102 and the LNG Canada expansion are genuine upside risks to Canadian inflation and activity, so the remaining edge is smaller and does not justify adding.

With no fresh dated United States path, stay flat.

pms.invalidation: Flatten the Canada receive if a Bank of Canada hike or hawkish path, especially with oil still three-digit, lifts March implieds back through 3.13 and holds them there. An official New Zealand 10-year print would allow a real reduce or close of the NZ-US short; until then do not invent an exit. positions.invalidation: Thesis fails if BoC hikes or the 1m CORRA strip through Dec-2026 reprices toward the 2027 CRA mid-3s; if CPI-trim/median leave the 1.9/2.0 zone higher while employment stops contracting and wages re-accelerate; or if CORRA_2027-03 implied holds at or above the 3.13 entry because catch-up is actually being delivered. A US-only or energy-headline move that leaves CRAH27 unchanged is not…
positions.thesis: That is the first 2027 three-month contract that prices a Canadian hiking cycle (+84bp vs CORRA cash 2.29) after 1m CORRA still only reaches 2.58 by Dec-2026 and Dec-26 3m CRAZ26 is 2.775. August labor (-42k, wages +2.0%) and CPI-trim/median 1.9/2.0 do not support delivering that 2027 path. Side long is duration-long in implied-rate space (profits if the 3.13 implied falls toward the still-alive near-term path).

positions.invalidation: Cover the CORRA receive if Bank of Canada 2027 hikes are delivered or the strip reprices back through the 3.13 entry, especially on a sticky oil-and-goods inflation impulse. Cover the NZ-US short if the 10-year spread cheapens further from minus 23 basis points toward richer New Zealand, including on an RBNZ easing surprise or a Treasury-led selloff that leaves New Zealand yields stuck.
positions.thesis: March 2027 CORRA still prices a full hike cycle versus 2.28 cash, so the existing receive remains the core book rather than a completed trade. Williams’ pushback on 2027 tightening supports that 2027 strips are the residual, but Canada already has the expression and the size. New Zealand 10s at 4.98 versus Treasuries at 5.21 is a first-percentile cheap-NZ dislocation and is the only overlay worth adding: pay New Zealand and receive US 10s, not more Canadian duration.

pms.thesis: The working book remains a received March 2027 Canada contract plus a short NZ-US 10-year residual that still has no official New Zealand 10-year print, so that second line can only be held. March Canada at 2.97 versus cash 2.49 still prices unused 2027 tightening, the receive is already through the 3.13 entry, and it still wants a lower mark even with oil at 117.64. A new March SOFR receive copies that same front-end easing beta while the desk is two-way, and a new US 10-year or dollar-yen ticket does not improve the Canada expression, so both live lines stay as they are.

pms.label: Grinder
pms.mandate: Preservation and consistency first. Smaller sizes, high hurdles, quick de-risking. No-trade is valid.
pms.thesis: Cash at the official overnight rate is the book. Receiving March SOFR after a hold, while the strip still marks Dec 4.13 through Sep 4.495 and Brent/WTI remain elevated, is a two-sided directional view rather than a preservation edge. The ten-year at 4.94 is a residual-cut story on an empty book; paying it from flat donates roughly a point of coupon versus cash unless yields sell off more than a spent hold and energy-driven inflation already allow, and receiving it fights that same inflation backdrop.
